1	# Migrating from react-docgen-typescript
2	
3	`oxc-react-docgen` targets output-shape compatibility with `react-docgen-typescript` (RDT) via the CLI's `--format rdt` flag. The NAPI binding and Vite plugin currently only expose this tool's own canonical format (`kind`-tagged `PropType`, shown in the main README) — no RDT-shape option at that layer yet.
4	
5	This document covers what's compatible today, what's intentionally different, and what's a known gap rather than a design choice.
6	
7	## Should you switch today?
8	
9	Output should match closely if your components use:
10	
11	- Plain interfaces or type aliases
12	- `forwardRef` (including wrapped in an `as` cast), `FC`, or HOC wrapping
13	- `Omit` / `Pick`
14	- `VariantProps` (CVA / TV / PandaCSS)
15	- Discriminated unions (including ones wrapped in an intersection)
16	
17	Scraping the full 250+ inherited HTML attributes per component? It's supported, but opt-in — see [HTML attribute inheritance](#html-attribute-inheritance) below.
18	
19	## Field-by-field comparison
20	
21	### Component level (`ComponentDoc`)
22	
23	| RDT field | `--format rdt` | Notes |
24	| --- | --- | --- |
25	| `displayName` | ✅ |  |
26	| `description` | ✅ | From the component's own leading JSDoc, if any |
27	| `props` | ✅ | See prop-level table below |
28	| `methods` | ✅ (always `[]`) | RDT only populates this for class components; we don't support class components, so it's always empty — present for shape compatibility, not because we detect methods |
29	| `tags` | ✅ | JSDoc `@tag` values on the component declaration (e.g. `@deprecated`, `@since`) — not part of RDT's original spec but included since some tooling reads it |
30	
31	### Prop level (`PropItem`)
32	
33	| RDT field | `--format rdt` | Notes |
34	| --- | --- | --- |
35	| `name` | ✅ |  |
36	| `required` | ✅ |  |
37	| `type.name` | ✅ | Literal unions emit `{name: "enum", value: [...]}` matching RDT's convention (so Storybook-style `<select>` controls activate) instead of inlining the literal text |
38	| `description` | ✅ |  |
39	| `defaultValue` | ✅ | `{value, computed}` — captured from destructured parameter defaults (`{ variant = 'primary' }`) or JSDoc `@default`, code value wins on conflict |
40	| `parent.name` / `parent.fileName` | ✅ | `fileName` is always canonicalized to an absolute path regardless of how `--src` was invoked |
41	| `declarations` | ❌ not emitted in `--format rdt` | Only present in `--format canonical` (the raw internal shape); omitted from both `--format rdt` and `--format storybook` to match RDT's single-parent shape. File an issue if you need it |
42	
43	### Intentionally omitted
44	
45	| Prop | Why |
46	| --- | --- |
47	| `ref` | Not a user-facing prop — a React internal. RDT includes it because it walks the full inherited type; we treat it as noise |
48	| `key` | Same reasoning as `ref` |
49	
50	### HTML attribute inheritance
51	
52	RDT inlines every inherited HTML attribute (e.g. all ~250-300 members of `ButtonHTMLAttributes`) directly into `props`. This tool doesn't, by default — set `--html-attributes` to control it:
53	
54	| Mode | Behavior | Reaches `--format rdt` |
55	| --- | --- | --- |
56	| `curated` (default) | ~15-20 commonly-documented attributes per element (`onClick`, `disabled`, `type`, ARIA attrs) in `notableInherited`. `inheritance` (canonical format only) still records the full layer — element, `Omit`-ted keys. | No |
57	| `full` | Resolves `@types/react`'s real `HTMLAttributes`/`AriaAttributes`/`DOMAttributes`/`<Element>HTMLAttributes` chain and merges it directly into `props`, matching RDT's flat behavior. | Yes |
58	| `none` | Own-declared props only. | Yes (nothing to add) |
59	
60	Flag by layer: `--html-attributes full` (CLI), `htmlAttributes: 'full'` (NAPI), `htmlAttributes: "full"` (`docgen.config.ts`).
61	
62	**`full` mode accuracy:** verified against a real button, 238 of ~250 real attributes resolve. The remainder is a narrow gap — a handful of `@types/react` fields reference a same-namespace sibling type without an explicit qualifier, which degrades to an `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` diagnostic on that one field rather than a crash or missing component. Details in `docs/rdt-coverage.md`'s "HtmlAttributeMode" section.
63	
64	If you need the full attribute set and aren't ready to opt into `full` mode, this is the main compatibility gap to check for your specific components.

content.text: Now the two dense methodology paragraphs at the top of "Output quality":

input.old_string:
"Coverage: N/M (X%)" was the only quality metric this repo had before this report — a raw prop-count ratio, not a real per-prop match rate, and it didn't account for known, deliberate design differences (see below). This section replaces it with a real per-prop agreement rate and a taxonomy of _why_ props disagree when they do, computed by `apps/validate/src/analyze.ts` from the same three tools' real output on all 21 fixture libraries (`apps/validate/fixtures/`).

**Methodology note — how each tool's type string is read:** `react-docgen-typescript` represents union/literal prop types as `{ name: 'enum', value: [...] }` — the real type string comes from `.value`, not `.name` (which is literally the string `"enum"`). `react-docgen` puts real TypeScript type info under `.tsType` (with a `.raw` field carrying the exact original source text), not `.type` (a legacy PropTypes-only field that's absent for TS-typed props). Both comparisons below read the real field on each side.

**Reading the aggregate percentage correctly:** a low agreement rate means different things against each comparator, and conflating them is the single easiest way to misread this report. Against RDT, low agreement means _this tool finds fewer props than RDT does_ — a real, directional gap (RDT has a type checker; see the outlier table below). Against react-docgen, low agreement mostly means the reverse — _this tool finds more than react-docgen does_, because react-docgen returns zero props for 45% of comparable components (see below) and everything this tool correctly extracts on top of that shows up as "extra," not as this tool being noisy or over-inclusive. The single percentage can't distinguish "we're missing things" from "the comparator is missing things" — that's why this section leads with the outlier table and the zero-props stat instead of the headline number.

content.text: Now the numbered list in "What this tool can provide that they can't" — items 1, 2, and 6 are dense single-paragraph entries:

input.old_string:
1. **Structured, typed degradation diagnostics.** Running this tool across all 21 fixture libraries produces **82 diagnostics** with typed codes (`UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT`: 30, `OPAQUE_TYPE`: 29, `INDEXED_ACCESS_OPAQUE`: 19, `DISCRIMINATED_UNION`: 2, `TEMPLATE_LITERAL_OPAQUE`: 2), file/line context, and human-readable help text (e.g. _"Enable typescript-go to resolve indexed access types."_). Neither RDT nor react-docgen tell you _why_ a prop came out wrong or missing — they silently omit it or print a generic parse error. This tool's non-negotiable #6 ("always emit a Diagnostic when degrading, never fail silently," `CLAUDE.md`) makes every gap in the tables above something a consumer's tooling can actually detect and act on, not something they discover by manually diffing output.
2. **`.d.ts`-only fixtures.** 8 of the 55 fixture files in this corpus (`mui`, `chakra`, `mantine`, `radix`, `react-aria`) are declaration-only — real published library type definitions with no accompanying `.tsx` source. **Neither RDT nor react-docgen can run on these at all** (both need a real component implementation to parse); this tool extracts full prop tables from them today, which is the entire reason it can validate against `node_modules`-vendored third-party types instead of only first-party source.
3. **Incremental extraction with a real API** (see the perf section above) — `WatchSession::update_file` for editor/HMR integration. RDT and react-docgen have nothing playing this role; the comparison isn't "we're faster at the same operation," it's "this operation doesn't exist for them."
4. **Cross-package monorepo import resolution** (`ImportResolutionMap`, barrel/re-export chain following, `extra_paths` workspace aliasing) — RDT resolves within a single `ts.Program`'s file set; getting it to follow a monorepo's package boundaries requires configuring that whole program correctly. This tool's import resolution is a first-class, independently-tested layer (`import_map.rs`, `resolver/import.rs`).
5. **Machine-consumable structured types**, not stringified type names. This tool's `PropType` is a real tagged union (`union`, `literalUnion`, `array`, `intersection`, `eventHandler`, ...) serialized as JSON — a consumer can programmatically ask "is this a union of string literals" without parsing a type string. RDT and react-docgen both hand back a printed type string (or in react-docgen's case, a partial tagged shape with a `.raw` escape hatch) as the primary representation.
6. **A `composes` field that actually gets populated.** `ComponentEntry.composes` is react-docgen's own documented mechanism for "these props come from a type we're not flattening — here's its name/expression" — but it existed unused for the type-checker-boundary failures above until this report found and fixed it. `base-ui/MenuTrigger` and all 3 `headlessui/Listbox` components now surface their real unresolvable expression (a mapped type, two conditional types) through `composes` in RDT-format output, instead of silently returning zero props with no trace. This is a stop-gap, not a fix for the underlying gap — 6 of the 10 outlier components (Ariakit, `ark-ui`, `storybook-emotion`, `fluentui`) still show empty `composes`, because their failure happens further upstream (generic-alias substitution not matching the pattern at all) than the one dead end this closed.

3	**Generated:** 2026-07-25.
4	
5	**Hardware:** Apple Silicon (arm64), macOS. Numbers below are absolute and will shift on different hardware — treat the _relative_ comparisons as the durable signal, not the absolute milliseconds.

They're measured differently on purpose — a fast tool that produces wrong output isn't actually useful, and this project's whole premise is "faster AND at least as accurate," so both get held to a real, reproducible standard here. 14	| `react-docgen-typescript` | 2.2.2     | full `ts.Program` + real TypeScript type checker |

27	Range (min … max):    44.1 ms …  70.4 ms    (48 runs, hyperfine, 3 warmup)
28	```
29	
30	### Cold extraction, all three tools under equal footing
31	
32	react-docgen and react-docgen-typescript can only run inside a Node process — there's no "direct binary" form for them to compare against. 33	
34	Two costs affect all three equally, plus one extra for us:
35	
36	- A `proto → pnpm → tsx → Node` startup tax, common to all three tools
37	- For `oxc-react-docgen` specifically: one extra child-process spawn on top of that, since the harness shells out to the compiled binary from inside that already-started Node process — the same way a real consumer's tooling would call it

40	| ------------------------- | -----------------: | ------: | -------: | -----------: |
41	| `oxc-react-docgen`        |  2.963 s ± 0.157 s | 2.759 s |  3.208 s |         1.00 |

45	(hyperfine, 10 runs each, 2 warmup runs)

28	| Conditional types (`T extends U ? A : B`) | Already emitted as `opaque` — correct behavior. Full evaluation requires the checker |
29	| Mapped types (`{ [K in keyof T]: ... }`) | Already emitted as `opaque` — correct behavior |
30	| Multi-level generic propagation | A chain like `type ButtonProps = ComponentProps<typeof Button>` where Button is defined elsewhere can be 3-4 hops; our import resolver follows same-file chains but cross-file generic substitution requires the type checker |
31	
32	---
33	
34	## TypeScript 7.0 / tsgo ecosystem status (as of 2026-06-28)
35	
36	### What happened
37	
38	TypeScript 7.0 RC shipped 2026-06-18. This is the Go rewrite of the compiler ("tsgo"), not a JavaScript refactor. The key changes:
39	
40	- **TypeScript 6.0** = last JavaScript-based tsc (maintenance only)
41	- **TypeScript 7.0** = Go rewrite; 10× build speed, same semantics
42	- **Strada API** (ts.createProgram, checker.getTypeAtLocation, LanguageService) = **completely dropped** in TS 7.0 — no shim, no compatibility layer
43	- **react-docgen-typescript** depends on Strada; it is **broken under TS 7.0**
44	
45	### Corsa API
46	
47	The tsgo team is building "Corsa" as the replacement public API. Status:
48	
49	- Corsa API: **not yet stable** — targeting TypeScript 7.1 (estimated late 2026 / early 2027)
50	- Current tsgo exports minimal surface: `check()`, `build()`, basic diagnostics
51	- No `getTypeAtLocation` equivalent yet
52	- Plugin system and language service extensions TBD
53	
54	### tsgolint precedent (OXC team)
55	
56	The OXC team already tackled cross-language integration with `tsgolint`:
57	
58	- Spawns `tsgo` as a subprocess
59	- Communicates via JSON IPC using tsgo's internal (unstable) shims
60	- This pattern works but depends on internal APIs that will break when Corsa lands
61	
62	We should NOT follow the tsgolint approach — it creates maintenance debt on an unstable internal API. Wait for Corsa.
63	
64	### Why oxc-react-docgen is unaffected by TS 7.0
65	
66	We parse TypeScript with OXC (Rust), not tsc. We have no dependency on the Strada API. Consumers running TS 7.0 can use oxc-react-docgen without any changes. This is a competitive advantage during the TS 6→7 migration window.
67	
68	---
69	
70	## Integration architecture (when Corsa is stable)
71	
72	The integration should be **opt-in**, not always-on. Most projects need only the structural analysis for prop documentation. The type checker adds latency (~100-500ms cold start) and a Node.js process dependency that many CI environments won't want.
73	
74	### Proposed design
75	
76	```
77	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
78	│  oxc-react-docgen  (current — always runs)              │
79	│  OXC AST parse → extractor → resolver → ExtractionOutput│
80	│  Props: structurally knowable types only                 │
81	│  Generics: emitted as PropType::Named or opaque         │
82	└──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
83	                           │ optional
84	                  ─────────▼─────────
85	                 │  Corsa enrichment  │
86	                 │  (future opt-in)   │
87	                 │                   │
88	                 │  For each prop     │
89	                 │  with opaque/Named │
90	                 │  type: call Corsa  │
91	                 │  getTypeAtLocation │
92	                 │  → replace with    │
93	                 │  resolved PropType │
94	                  ───────────────────
95	```
96	
97	**CLI flag:** `--with-type-checker` (default: off) **Config key:** `docgen.config.ts → typeChecker: true | { path: string }` **Node requirement:** Node 22+ (tsgo ships as npm package)
98	
99	### Specific Corsa operations needed
100	
101	When the Corsa API is available, the following operations unblock the deferred gaps:
102	
103	| Operation                                  | Corsa API (expected)                      | Gap resolved               |
104	| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
105	| Resolve generic type argument at call site | `checker.getTypeArguments(typeRef)`       | Generic param substitution |
106	| Evaluate conditional type                  | `checker.resolveConditionalType(node)`    | Conditional opaque         |
107	| Expand mapped type                         | `checker.getIndexedAccessType(type, key)` | Mapped opaque              |
108	| Follow `typeof expr`                       | `checker.getTypeOfExpression(expr)`       | typeof depth               |
109	
110	The integration point is `resolver/chain.rs:resolve_props_chain` — after step 5 fails to find the interface in our global map, step 6 currently emits an `UnresolvableImport` diagnostic. With Corsa, a step 5.5 would ask the type checker for the props instead.
111	
112	### File plan (future)
113	
114	```
115	crates/core/src/typechecker/          (new module, feature-gated)
116	  mod.rs              — feature gate, public API surface
117	  corsa_bridge.rs     — subprocess IPC with tsgo/Corsa
118	  prop_enricher.rs    — walk ExtractionOutput, replace opaque props
119	```
120	
121	Feature gate: `cargo build --features=type-checker` — keeps the no-Node-dependency build path as the default.
122	
123	---
124	
125	## Timeline
126	
127	| Milestone                               | When              | What it unlocks                                      |
128	| --------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
129	| TS 7.0 RC                               | 2026-06-18 (done) | Confirms Strada is dropped; competitive window opens |
130	| TS 7.1 release candidate                | ~Q4 2026          | Corsa API draft; begin bridge prototype              |
131	| TS 7.1 stable + Corsa stable            | ~Q1 2027          | Implement generic substitution, `typeof` depth       |
132	| Public release of `--with-type-checker` | ~Q1 2027          | Feature-complete RDT replacement                     |
133	
134	Until then: fix the 5 structural gaps (see implementation plan), ship, and let users migrate to oxc-react-docgen during the TS 7 disruption window.
135

1	# oxc-react-docgen
2	
3	React component prop extraction powered by [OXC](https://oxc.rs). Parses TypeScript natively in Rust — no TypeScript compiler program, no type-checking pass, no startup tax.
4	
5	> **Status:** Core extraction, NAPI bindings, Vite plugin, CLI, and `docgen.config.ts` loading are complete.
6	
7	## Why
8	
9	`react-docgen-typescript` spins up a full TypeScript `Program` to extract props. On a mid-size design system that takes seconds — enough to noticeably delay Storybook startup and make HMR feel sluggish.
10	
11	OXC parses each file in parallel with no type-checking pass:
12	
13	- **Cold extraction, 21 real component libraries:** 50ms ([full breakdown](docs/benchmarks.md))
14	- **Incremental single-file update:** ~2ms — react-docgen-typescript has no equivalent API; every edit re-pays the full cold cost
15	
16	The CLI can emit an RDT-compatible shape via `--format rdt` (see [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md)). The Vite plugin and NAPI binding currently expose this tool's own canonical format only — not a drop-in RDT replacement at that layer yet.
17	
18	## Install
19	
20	> Not yet on npm. No prebuilt per-platform binaries exist yet — build from source:
21	
22	```bash
23	git clone https://github.com/orin-dx/oxc-react-docgen
24	cd oxc-react-docgen
25	pnpm install
26	pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/napi run build:napi   # builds the native addon for your platform
27	pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin build
28	```
29	
30	Use `pnpm run build:napi`, not a bare `cargo build` — it invokes `napi build`, which places the compiled addon exactly where `packages/napi/index.js`'s loader expects it.
31	
32	Migrating off `react-docgen-typescript`? See [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md) for what's compatible today.
33	
34	## Vite plugin
35	
36	```ts
37	// vite.config.ts
38	import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
39	import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
40	import { oxcReactDocgen } from '@oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin'
41	
42	export default defineConfig({
43	  plugins: [react(), oxcReactDocgen({ srcDirs: ['src'] })],
44	})
45	```
46	
47	Metadata is available on the `virtual:oxc-react-docgen` module and pushed via HMR as components change:
48	
49	```ts
50	import docgen from 'virtual:oxc-react-docgen'
51	
52	docgen.components['Button'].props
53	// {
54	//   variant: {
55	//     type: { kind: 'literalUnion', members: ['default', 'destructive', 'outline'], hasDefault: true },
56	//     required: false,
57	//     defaultValue: { value: '"default"', computed: false },
58	//     description: '',
59	//   },
60	//   ...
61	// }
62	```
63	
64	## CLI
65	
66	A single Rust binary (`crates/cli`) — argument parsing, output formatting, and `--format rdt`/`--format storybook` serialization all live there. `@oxc-react-docgen/cli` (once published) is a thin npm wrapper that execs the platform-appropriate compiled binary — no reimplemented logic, so there's exactly one place CLI behavior can drift.
67	
68	```bash
69	# Once published: npx @oxc-react-docgen/cli extract --src src/ --out docgen.json
70	# From source today: ./target/release/oxc-react-docgen (after cargo build --release)
71	
72	# One-shot extraction
73	oxc-react-docgen extract --src src/ --out docgen.json
74	
75	# Inspect a single file
76	oxc-react-docgen inspect src/components/Button.tsx
77	
78	# Watch mode
79	oxc-react-docgen watch --src src/
80	
81	# Shell completions
82	oxc-react-docgen completions zsh > ~/.zsh/completions/_oxc-react-docgen
83	
84	# Full HTML attribute expansion instead of the default curated subset
85	oxc-react-docgen extract --src src/ --html-attributes full
86	```
87	
88	Settings can also live in `docgen.config.ts` (`srcDirs`, `htmlAttributes`, `reactVersion`, `crossPackage`, and more — see `crates/cli/src/config.rs` for the full schema) instead of CLI flags.
89	
90	## Output shape
91	
92	```json
93	{
94	  "components": {
95	    "Button": {
96	      "displayName": "Button",
97	      "filePath": "src/components/Button.tsx",
98	      "props": {
99	        "variant": {
100	          "type": { "kind": "literalUnion", "members": ["default", "destructive", "outline"], "hasDefault": true },
101	          "required": false,
102	          "defaultValue": { "value": "\"default\"", "computed": false },
103	          "description": "Visual style variant.",
104	          "tags": {}
105	        }
106	      },
107	      "inheritance": [
108	        { "typeName": "ButtonHTMLAttributes", "htmlElement": "button", "omitted": [], "totalProps": 147 }
109	      ],
110	      "notableInherited": {
111	        "onClick": { "type": { "kind": "eventHandler", "eventType": "MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>" }, ... },
112	        "disabled": { "type": { "kind": "boolean" }, ... }
113	      },
114	      "discriminantProp": null
115	    }
116	  },
117	  "diagnostics": [],
118	  "stats": { "filesParsed": 3, "durationMs": 12, "dtsCacheHits": 2, ... }
119	}
120	```
121	
122	## Supported patterns
123	
124	| Pattern                    | Example                                                           |
125	| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
126	| Function components        | `function Button(props: ButtonProps)`                             |
127	| Arrow components           | `const Button = (props: ButtonProps) => ...`                      |
128	| `React.forwardRef`         | `forwardRef<HTMLButtonElement, ButtonProps>(...)`                 |
129	| HOC-wrapped                | `styled(Base)<ButtonProps>`                                       |
130	| Interface inheritance      | `interface ButtonProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>` |
131	| Intersection aliases       | `type ButtonProps = BaseProps & { variant?: string }`             |
132	| `Omit` / `Pick`            | `type ButtonProps = Omit<InputProps, 'value'>`                    |
133	| `ComponentPropsWithoutRef` | `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'button'>`                              |
134	| `VariantProps`             | `VariantProps<typeof buttonVariants>` (CVA / TV / PandaCSS)       |
135	| Discriminated unions       | MUI-style `variant: 'filled' \| 'outlined' \| 'standard'`         |
136	| JSDoc tags                 | `@description`, `@default`, `@deprecated`, `@internal`            |
137	
138	## Repository
139	
140	```
141	crates/core/          pure extraction logic (no I/O, no async, Send + Sync)
142	crates/binding/       thin NAPI wrapper over core
143	crates/cli/           clap + miette CLI
144	packages/napi/        @oxc-react-docgen/napi (dev binary loader + TS types)
145	packages/vite-plugin/ @oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin
146	packages/cli/         @oxc-react-docgen/cli (npx wrapper — execs crates/cli's binary, no reimplemented logic)
147	apps/validate/        accuracy comparison harness (react-docgen, rdt, ours)
148	fixtures/             real library .d.ts/.tsx files (shadcn, MUI, Chakra, Mantine, etc.)
149	```
150	
151	## Contributing
152	
153	[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — setup, code style, commit conventions.  
154	[ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) — pipeline, modules, key design decisions.
155	
156	## License
157	
158	AGPL-3.0-or-later — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

Investigate whether this repo has a Cargo-workspace build-lock serialization bug in its
CI/lint/test task runner (moon, Turborepo, Nx, Makefile, or similar), and fix it if so.

## Background

Cargo takes a process-level file lock on a workspace's shared `target/` directory for the
duration of any `cargo` invocation (build, check, clippy, test) touching it. If a monorepo
task runner fans out one `cargo <cmd> -p $crate` invocation per crate — even when it *thinks*
it's running them in parallel — every one of those processes contends for the same lock, so
they serialize behind each other. The task runner's own parallelism is real at the process-
spawn level; Cargo silently defeats it underneath. Symptom: a lint/build/test step that "hangs"
or takes 10-60+ minutes even though no single crate should take that long, with repeated
"Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory" lines in verbose output — easy to
misdiagnose as a hung process, a bad dependency (heavy C-linked crates like aws-lc-sys/ring/
wasmtime are common red herrings), or a caching bug, when it's actually just N processes
queued behind one lock.

This is a known, acknowledged Cargo/monorepo-tool interaction — moonrepo's own Rust handbook
states it explicitly: "if you do per-crate, Cargo itself will 'wait for build lock' when
multiple processes are running," and recommends workspace-wide invocations instead.

## Diagnose

1. Find the task definition that runs clippy/build/test per-crate (e.g. a global task template
   with `-p $project` or equivalent, applied to every package).
2. Run the full task with verbose/streaming output and check for repeated
   "Blocking waiting for file lock" lines, and whether wall-clock time is roughly the *sum* of
   each crate's individual build time rather than the *max*.
3. Confirm: kill everything, run one crate's task alone and time it, then run the full fan-out
   and compare total wall time against (that time) × (crate count). If they're close, this is
   the bug.

## Fix

Two changes, not one — they serve different call sites:

1. **Full-scope runs (CI, `just ci`-equivalent):** replace the per-crate fan-out with a single
   `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (same pattern for `build`/`test`,
   though `cargo test --workspace` doesn't run doctests — pair with `cargo test --doc`, or use
   `cargo nextest run --workspace` and fall back to the runner's own task for coverage it
   doesn't handle). One process, Cargo's internal job scheduler parallelizes compilation across
   crates on its own — no lock contention because there's only one lock-holder.

2. **Affected-only runs (pre-push, incremental CI):** don't drop the task runner's affected-
   project detection — it's real, dependency-graph-aware signal a plain Cargo invocation can't
   compute on its own. Instead of letting it *execute* per-project (which reintroduces the same
   lock problem at a smaller scale whenever 2+ projects are affected), use it only to *build the
   scope*, then feed that into one Cargo invocation with multiple `-p` flags:
   projects=$(<task-runner query for affected project ids>)
   if [ -z "$projects" ]; then exit 0; fi
   args=(); for p in $projects; do args+=(-p "$p"); done
   cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets -- -D warnings
For moon specifically: `moon query projects --affected` returns JSON with a `.projects[].id`
array of exactly the changed crates (verified: touching two crates' files returns exactly
those two project ids, nothing else) — pipe that through `jq -r '.projects[].id'`.

Do not scope lint to affected crates' *downstream dependents* — clippy warnings are about a
crate's own source, not its callers, so only the changed crates themselves need relinting. Test
scoping is a separate, judgment-call question (a changed crate's behavior can break a
downstream crate's integration tests) — don't fold that into a lint fix without deciding it
explicitly.

## Verify

- Time the old fan-out path once for a real before/after number, not just "it feels faster."
- Test both the zero-affected case (clean tree → instant no-op) and a multi-affected case
  (touch 2+ unrelated crates → confirm the resulting single command lints exactly those crates
  and nothing else) before trusting the fix.
- Re-run the repo's full CI/lint suite once after the change to confirm nothing else broke.

name: CI
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

# Cancel in-progress runs for the same branch/PR.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1

jobs:
  # Computes which projects (per moon's project graph, including transitive
  # dependents — a crates/core change correctly marks crates/cli, crates/binding,
  # and packages/napi as affected too) changed relative to the base ref, so
  # untouched language groups can skip their jobs entirely. Fails open (treats
  # everything as affected) on any error or unusual ref — a skipped real check
  # is a much worse failure mode than an unnecessary one.
  detect-changes:
    name: Detect affected projects
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      rust: ${{ steps.detect.outputs.rust }}
      typescript: ${{ steps.detect.outputs.typescript }}
      docs: ${{ steps.detect.outputs.docs }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@v0
      - id: detect
        run: |
          set +e
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "pull_request" ]; then
            BASE="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          else
            BASE="${{ github.event.before }}"
          fi

          # No usable base (first push to a branch, force-push, etc.) — run everything.
          if [ -z "$BASE" ] || [ "$BASE" = "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" ] || ! git cat-file -e "$BASE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "rust=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "typescript=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "No usable base ref — running everything."
            exit 0
          fi

          # Markdown isn't a moon project — moon's affected-project graph below has
          # no way to flag a docs-only change, so it's detected separately here with
          # a plain path diff instead of folding it into the rust/typescript logic.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE" -- '*.md' | grep -q .; then
            echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "docs=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

          # moon 2.3.3's `query projects` has no --base/--head flags (confirmed against
          # `moon query projects --help` and the pinned version) — passing them failed
          # the whole command, which used to silently land in the fail-open branch below
          # every single run. It reads the base from MOON_BASE instead, and always diffs
          # against whatever's actually checked out on disk (there's no MOON_HEAD — moon
          # ignores it if set) — which is exactly github.sha here since actions/checkout
          # already put us there, so this is the correct comparison without needing one.
          AFFECTED=$(MOON_BASE="$BASE" moon query projects --affected --downstream deep)
          if [ $? -ne 0 ] || [ -z "$AFFECTED" ]; then
            echo "rust=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "typescript=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "moon query failed — running everything."
            exit 0
          fi

          IDS=$(echo "$AFFECTED" | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(' '.join(p['id'] for p in d['projects']))")
          echo "Affected projects: ${IDS:-none}"

          RUST=false
          TS=false
          for id in $IDS; do
            case "$id" in
              core|cli|crates-binding) RUST=true ;;
              vite-plugin|napi|validate|cli-npm) TS=true ;;
              # Unmapped project (new one added to .moon/workspace.yml and forgotten
              # here) — fail open rather than silently leaving it with zero CI coverage.
              *) RUST=true; TS=true ;;
            esac
          done

          echo "rust=$RUST" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "typescript=$TS" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # ── Rust ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  lint:
    name: Lint
    needs: detect-changes
    if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.rust == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.96.0
        with:
          components: clippy, rustfmt
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - run: cargo fmt --check
      - run: cargo clippy --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked -- -D warnings

  test:
    name: Test
    needs: detect-changes
    if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.rust == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.96.0
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@nextest
      - run: cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked

  deny:
    name: Deny (licenses · advisories · bans)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action@v2

  coverage:
    name: Coverage
    needs: detect-changes
    if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.rust == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

      - uses: codecov/codecov-action@v5
        with:
          files: lcov.info
          fail_ci_if_error: false

content.text: No affected-only fan-out bug exists here — CI's affected-detection is already coarse (whole-workspace or skip, never per-crate `-p` fan-out), so that part of the prescribed fix doesn't apply. The two real broken call sites are `justfile`'s `build` recipe and `package.json`'s `build`/`test`/`lint` scripts. `just` itself isn't a pinned/proto-managed tool, so I won't make `package.json` depend on it — fixing both directly with raw workspace-wide commands, matching the pattern `just lint`/`just test`/CI already use safely.

input.old_string:
# Build all projects
build:
    moon run :build
    cargo build --release
input.new_string:
# Build all projects. Rust crates build via one workspace-wide cargo
# invocation, not `moon run :build` — that fans out one `cargo build -p`
# per crate, and every one of those processes contends for the same
# target/ file lock, serializing what moon's own scheduler thinks is
# parallel work (confirmed via `Blocking waiting for file lock` in verbose
# output). napi/vite-plugin have no such lock to contend over, so moon
# still orchestrates those directly.
build:
    cargo build --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi
    moon run napi:build vite-plugin:build
    cargo build --release

content.text:
**Confirmed: real bug, now fixed.**

**Diagnosis:** `moon run :build`/`:test`/`:lint` (used by `justfile`'s `build` recipe and root `package.json`'s `build`/`test`/`lint` scripts) fan out per-crate `cargo build/clippy/nextest -p <crate>` across `crates/core`, `crates/cli`, `crates/binding` — each a separate process contending for the same `target/` lock. Reproduced live: a clean `moon run :build` showed `cli:build` and `crates-binding:build` racing (both depend only on `core:build`), with repeated `Blocking waiting for file lock on package cache`/`on build directory` — `cli:build` sat blocked until `crates-binding:build` released the lock. Total: 17.9s. CI's actual gate and `just ci`/`lint`/`test` were already safe — they call `cargo ... --workspace` directly, never through moon's per-project fan-out.

**Fix:**
- `justfile`'s `build` recipe: replaced `moon run :build` with `cargo build --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi`, then `moon run napi:build vite-plugin:build` for the two TS-side steps that still need moon's dependency graph (no cargo lock involved there).
- `package.json`'s `build`/`test`/`lint`: same pattern — direct workspace-wide `cargo` invocations, with `test` also running vite-plugin's vitest suite directly via `pnpm --filter`.
- No affected-only fan-out bug existed to fix — CI's affected-detection is already coarse (whole Rust workspace or skip, never per-crate `-p`), so that part of the described fix pattern didn't apply here.

**Verified:** same clean-rebuild scenario after the fix — 11.9s, only a brief solo lock touch (not contention between two racing processes). `pnpm lint` (529... wait, that's test) clean clippy across both crates; `pnpm test` — 529 Rust tests + 33 vitest tests, all green. `just ci` now gets past `fmt`/`clippy` cleanly; it still fails on pre-existing markdown-format debt in 17 unrelated files (not something I introduced or am fixing here).

Nothing committed. Changed: `justfile`, `package.json`, `docs/benchmarks.md` (unrelated regression fix from the earlier docs pass). The Callisto release-prep files from a prior task remain untouched and still uncommitted.

Can we take a look at the current setup for callisto at ~/Projects and see what else we should adjust in terms of moon, cargo or any of our ecosystem setup? Summarize what you find and a proposal.

  This is what michi learned:

  Callisto setup vs. michi's

  Surveyed ~/Projects/callisto (orin-dx/callisto's own repo — same moon+cargo+changesets stack, more mature/battle-tested). Two categories of findings.

  1. A live bug in callisto itself (worth knowing, not michi's to fix)

  callisto's own justfile already has the exact same fix I just applied to michi — lint (single cargo clippy --workspace) + lint-affected (moon-affected-detection → single multi--p invocation), with near-identical comments explaining the lock-contention problem. So callisto's maintainers hit and fixed this before.

  But .github/workflows/callisto-release.yml never got the memo — it calls moon run :format-check/moon run :lint/moon run :test directly, bypassing the fixed justfile recipes entirely. Callisto's own .moon/tasks/rust.yml still defines the raw per-crate -p $project fan-out tasks (dormant, unlike michi's now-deleted ones), so every release-verification run on callisto still pays the lock-serialization tax. callisto-ci.yml (the main CI) correctly uses just lint/just fmt-check/just test — only the release workflow regressed. Michi's own release.yml is unaffected — it calls orin-dx/callisto's callisto-action, which runs callisto status/version/publish directly, never moon run :*.

  2. Patterns callisto has that michi doesn't

  Centralized lints (highest value) — callisto declares lint policy once, in root Cargo.toml:
  [workspace.lints.rust]
  unsafe_code = "forbid"
  unused_must_use = "deny"
  [workspace.lints.clippy]
  all = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
  map_err_ignore = "deny"
  then each crate opts in with one line: [lints] / workspace = true. Michi instead has this exact block hand-copied at the top of all six lib.rs files:
  #![deny(unsafe_code)]
  #![warn(missing_docs)]
  #![warn(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used)]
  #![warn(clippy::disallowed_types)]
  Same policy, 6x duplicated, invisible from Cargo.toml, and drifts silently if one file gets updated and the others don't. Rust 1.74+ feature (michi's MSRV is 1.96) — straightforward to consolidate. One nuance: michi's unsafe_code needs to stay deny (overridable), not callisto's forbid, since CLAUDE.md explicitly allows unsafe at the NAPI boundary via local #[allow].

  cargo-semver-checks — callisto runs cargo semver-checks check-release as just check-api. Michi has no mechanical enforcement of its own documented SemVer contract (docs/spec/05-scope-and-quality.md's Patch/Minor/Major table) — which is exactly the gap that let four breaking changes land without changesets this session. This is the single highest-leverage addition given what we just found.

  cargo-machete — unused-dependency check, cheap to add, no downside.

  cargo-mutants as a standing just mutants recipe — michi already gets mutation testing during implementation via the lambda:mutator agent skill, but it's not a repeatable local/CI gate the way callisto has it. Lower priority — already partially covered.

  Not relevant to michi: callisto's .moon/tasks/callisto.yml (dogfooding its own CLI) and its heavier wasm-check (building a real Extism/wasmtime plugin) — those are specific to callisto being a moon plugin, not applicable here.

  ---

  Proposal

  1. Add cargo-semver-checks — just check-api recipe + CI job, gates on the SemVer contract already documented. Directly closes the gap this session surfaced.
  2. Consolidate lints — move the 6x-duplicated #![...] block into [workspace.lints] + [lints] workspace = true per crate, keeping unsafe_code = "deny" (not forbid).
  3. Add cargo-machete — cheap unused-dep hygiene check.
  4. (Optional, lower priority) just mutants recipe for on-demand mutation sweeps outside the agent workflow.

  Want me to implement any of these now? I'd suggest #1 first given it's directly tied to the changeset gap we just found.

# Default recipe: run full CI pipeline via moon & just
default: ci

# Build debug workspace binaries via moon
build:

# Run unit, integration, doctests, and E2E tests
test:

# Run Clippy lints (warnings treated as errors) as a single workspace invocation.
# Moon's per-project `cargo clippy -p $project` tasks all lock the same shared
# target/ dir, so running them one-per-project serializes on Cargo's own build
# lock instead of parallelizing — a single --workspace invocation lets Cargo's
# internal job scheduler parallelize across crates instead.
lint:
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

# Lint only projects affected by changes since the base branch. Uses moon's
# project graph to find affected crates, then lints them in one cargo
# invocation (not moon's per-project fan-out) to avoid Cargo's build-lock
# serialization while still skipping unaffected crates entirely.
lint-affected:

    set -euo pipefail
    projects=$(moon query projects --affected 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.projects[].id')
    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then
        echo "No projects affected — skipping lint."
        exit 0
    fi
    args=()
    for p in $projects; do args+=(-p "$p"); done
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets -- -D warnings

content.text:
Surveyed `~/projects/callisto` directly (not just trusting the pasted report) and compared against our own current state.

**Validated, not new:** callisto's own `justfile` has the identical `lint` + `lint-affected` fix pattern I just applied here — independent confirmation the approach is right.

**The `callisto-release.yml` bug is real but doesn't touch us.** Confirmed: `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml:27-33` still calls `moon run :format-check/:lint/:test` directly, and `.moon/tasks/rust.yml` still defines the dormant per-crate `-p $project` fan-out. But I checked `callisto-action/action.yml` (what *our* `release.yml` actually calls) — it never invokes `moon run :*` internally, only mentions it as an example string for the `publish` input. We're not exposed. FYI-only, not an action item.

**Gaps I found in our own setup, checked against callisto's:**

| Pattern | Callisto | Us | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[workspace.lints]` | Centralized, `unsafe_code = "forbid"` | `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` duplicated in `core`/`cli` (2x, not 6x like michi) | Same drift risk, smaller blast radius. Consolidate; use `"deny"` not `"forbid"` — `crates/binding` needs unsafe for the NAPI FFI boundary and currently has neither, so `forbid` can't be locally overridden there but `deny` can. |
| `cargo-semver-checks` | `just check-api` | Not installed | **Premature for us** — zero releases exist yet, nothing to diff against. Defer until v0.1.0's first real crates.io publish (ties into the still-uncommitted Callisto release-prep work), not now. |
| `cargo-machete` | `just machete` | Not installed | Cheap, no downside, add it. |
| `cargo-mutants` gate | `just mutants` | Binary installed locally, no recipe | Low priority — same as michi, already loosely covered by ad hoc agent use. |
| Doc-check (`RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc`) + `cargo test --doc` | Both present | **Neither exists** — confirmed `nextest` (our test runner) silently never runs doctests, and there's no CI doc gate at all | Not in the michi report, but a real gap here. Cheap, catches real breakage today (no doctests exist yet, so zero risk to land), doesn't need a release to matter. |
| Native git hooks | Hand-rolled `just hooks` script | moon's own `hooks:` block in `.moon/workspace.yml` | We're already ahead here — no change needed. |

**Proposal, ranked for this repo specifically (differs from michi's ranking):**

1. **Doc-check gate** — `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace` + `cargo test --doc --workspace` as a `just doc-check` recipe + CI step. Cheapest, immediately useful, no release dependency.
2. **Consolidate lints** — `[workspace.lints.rust] unsafe_code = "deny"` + `[lints] workspace = true` on `core`/`cli` (not `binding`).
3. **`cargo-machete`** — cheap hygiene check.
4. **`cargo-semver-checks`** — defer, document as a follow-up tied to the first real publish.
5. *(Optional)* `just mutants` recipe.

Want me to implement 1–3 now?

**Publish order now accounts for dev-dependencies between same-batch packages**

- **Fixed:** `cargo publish` (run without `--no-verify`) rebuilds the packaged tarball to verify it, which needs every declared dependency -- including `[dev-dependencies]` -- resolvable from the registry. Publish ordering previously ignored dev-dependency edges entirely, so a package with a dev-dependency on a same-batch sibling could be published before that sibling, failing with an unresolvable version requirement.
- Dev-dependency ordering is best-effort, not a hard requirement: a legitimate mutual dev-dependency between two otherwise-unrelated packages no longer risks hard-failing the whole publish plan -- it falls back to the previous (non-dev) ordering for that case instead.

cd /Users/gabe/Projects/oxc-react-codegen
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix: eliminate Cargo build-lock serialization in moon-driven full builds

`just build` and the root package.json's build/test/lint scripts ran
`moon run :build`/`:test`/`:lint`, which fans out one `cargo build/
clippy/nextest -p <crate>` per Rust crate. Every one of those processes
contends for the same target/ file lock, so moon's parallelism was
illusory — the crates serialized behind Cargo's own lock. Reproduced
live: `cli:build` sat blocked on `crates-binding:build`'s lock for the
full run (17.9s), with repeated "Blocking waiting for file lock" lines.

Replaced with a single workspace-wide cargo invocation per full run,
letting Cargo's own job scheduler parallelize compilation across crates
instead of moon's process-level fan-out. napi/vite-plugin still go
through moon — no Cargo lock involved there. Confirmed fix: same clean
rebuild, 11.9s, no contention. CI's own gate and `just ci`/`lint`/`test`
were never affected — they already called `cargo ... --workspace`
directly, bypassing moon's per-project tasks.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -8
git log --oneline -2
